core_aesthetic_takeaways: The batch is valuable for city identity systems that need a parent mark, sublogos, dynamic variants, and construction logic.
The strongest transferable pattern is not a single style, but the method: one skeleton, many controlled variants.
Place symbols should be abstracted through grid, node, letter, pixel, or local-feature rules instead of literal landmark stacking.
Use the batch to avoid generic municipal logos by requiring a repeatable identity grammar before color or landmark decoration.
prompt_structure_lessons: Start city identity prompts by defining the public entity, parent mark skeleton, and sublogo logic.
Describe whether the system uses modular blocks, faceted polygons, grid icons, pixels, nodes, or typographic lines.
Require a variant grid and small-size legibility proof before final logo rendering.
Separate exact city name text from logo-structure training.

requires_source_confirmation: all official city or township names
text_accuracy_policy.training_rule: Use this batch for logo system grammar and city identity methods. Do not copy official marks, exact public names, or campaign slogans unless the user supplies and authorizes the text.

risk_controls.mitigation: Treat marks and names as reference-only. Generate new city identities from abstracted grammar, not from exact mark replication.
Require one parent skeleton and a derivation rule before adding local references.
Keep all variants tied to a shared grid, node map, letter skeleton, or color system.
Exact city names, office names and slogans must be supplied by the user.

recommended_training_use.stage_1_curation: include as a public-cultural-communication and vi-brand positive reference after rights review
recommended_training_use.stage_2_caption_tuning: use captions to teach parent-child city identity systems, dynamic logo families, and grid-derived place symbols
recommended_training_use.stage_3_lora_training: train as a civic identity subset before mixing with commercial brand VI or packaging cases
